items.title: OpenAI ships GPT-Live-1 in the API, Speak reports 80% fewer interruptions
items.summary: OpenAI launched GPT-Live-1 in general availability on September 10, a full-duplex voice model that listens and speaks at the same time and can hand reasoning/tool calls off to a backend model like GPT-6 Astra. It costs $0.05/minute for the voice layer, ships with 12 voices, and lists French among its native-quality-fluency languages at launch alongside English, Spanish, Mandarin, Japanese, and German. Language app Speak is a named launch partner: its CTO reported GPT-Live-1 cut mid-sentence interruptions during learners' thinking pauses by about 80% versus its prior turn-based system.
items.whyItMatters: Full-duplex listen-while-speaking is exactly the architecture problem behind Romain's turn-taking with hesitant French learners, and Speak's own numbers on a live language-tutor product are the closest real-world benchmark yet for whether switching off a chained STT-LLM-TTS pipeline is worth it.

items.title: Gemini Live adds an in-conversation live-translation toggle, French included
items.summary: Google is rolling out a "Turn on live translation" option inside Gemini Live's voice settings on Android, letting the assistant detect spoken words in another language and translate them on the fly with on-screen captions as the conversation continues. It ships alongside minor UI tweaks (a clearer exit button, on-screen interruption prompts) in a gradual server-side rollout reported September 10, building on Gemini's broader Live Translate feature that already covers French among its 70+ supported languages.
items.whyItMatters: A captioned, always-listening live-translation toggle inside an ordinary voice-assistant UI is a direct product-design reference for a fallback "help me understand" mode inside Romain or Anna when a learner gets stuck mid-sentence.

items.title: OpenAI opens the Agents API in public beta, exposing the Codex harness
items.summary: OpenAI launched the Agents API in public beta on September 10, putting the same session/orchestration/context-compaction harness that powers Codex behind a single API call. It supports MCP connections, sandboxed code and file-editing execution (OpenAI-managed, self-hosted, or partner sandboxes), and multi-agent delegation, with no extra fee beyond model tokens and paid tools.
items.whyItMatters: A managed harness for juggling conversation state, tool calls, and multi-agent delegation could simplify the backend orchestration behind Romain/Anna's session logic (grammar lookups, progress tracking) without hand-rolling that plumbing.

items.title: ElevenLabs signs its first major-label deal, with Universal Music Group
items.summary: Universal Music Group and ElevenLabs announced a multi-year licensing agreement on September 10 to build a fan-facing AI music co-creation platform for remixes, mashups, and "personalized vocal experiences" using UMG artists' catalogs. It's ElevenLabs' first agreement with a major label, sitting separately from its existing Music API and ElevenMusic products, with no launch date yet.
items.whyItMatters: Not a tutoring feature, but a data point on ElevenLabs' commercial trajectory and rights-clearing playbook as a vendor Anna's stack depends on for TTS.
